summary: I sent the exact brief with no visual cues. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md and the four UI guideline docs. The conversation was auto-compacted, and the skill was restored ("Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)"). The agent then said "This looks bounded… short design here in chat rather than write a spec". On its own it ran scripts/start-server.sh, gave a localhost URL with a key, and wrote filter-placement.html with three layout mockups (A: filter bar, B: popover, C: quick views). It asked for my reaction in the terminal. I picked A. It asked which controls to include and two non-visual questions in the terminal, posted the design in chat, and waited for my "yes". After I approved, it started implementation prep by re-reading the guidelines. No spec or plan file was created.
reasoning: All 8 criteria were met. Even after an auto-compaction, the agent decided on its own (with no visual cue from me) to open the visual companion at the moment the layout question came up. It kept the task bounded with the design in chat, created no spec or plan, asked for approval before writing code, and started implementation after I approved. The session log and filesystem checks match what the screen showed.

observations.description: Startup dialogs: the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions prompts both default to "No, exit". There was also an 'Update to Opus 5.5?' prompt even though the launcher already passes --model claude-opus-5-5, and the footer said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'. I answered No, and the session header then showed Opus 5.5.

Auto-compaction happened at least twice in a short session (two compact_boundary events, plus a third 'Skills restored' after approval). The four long guideline docs fill the context fast. After compacting, the agent re-reads the guidelines, so it spent extra turns reading after approval before any edit.

The mockup and the design text say 'Showing 4 of 311 events', but the fixture's activity-data.js has 48 events. The number 311 comes from NOTES.md, probably the live endpoint figure. This could confuse a user looking at the mockup.

The agent added a note that the companion is 'token-intensive, so say the word if you'd rather keep things in the terminal'. That's a helpful opt-out. It also advised adding .hyperpowers/ to .gitignore, which is good.

After I picked the filter bar, the agent asked three more AskUserQuestion prompts (controls, no-JS gap, tokens) before posting the design. That's reasonable, but the tokens and no-JS questions come from the agent's own reading of the guidelines rather than the user's needs. It's a bit heavy for a bounded task.

criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in the session log is Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) Successfully loaded skill" right after my brief.

Log has a Bash call: "bash …/skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir \"$PWD\" --open". The screen showed "http://localhost:56661/?key=5923…". The file .hyperpowers/brainstorm/56177-1793834612/content/filter-placement.html (5616 bytes) contains "

Where should the filters go on the account activity page?

" with mockups for options A, B and C.

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time; non-visual questions not routed through browser
criteria.evidence: Tool order in the log: Skill, then reading notes, guidelines and visual-companion.md, then start-server.sh, then Write filter-placement.html. Nothing was announced before the layout question came up ("Adding filters raises a question about where they go, so I'll sketch that in a browser tab"). After my pick it wrote waiting.html ("Continuing in terminal..."). It asked the controls, no-JS and tokens questions in the terminal with AskUserQuestion.

Screen and log text: "This looks bounded: it's a filter on a page that already exists. So I'll give you a short design here in chat rather than write a spec." Its AskUserQuestion options even noted that some choices would move the task "off the bounded path".

`find . -path ./.git -prune -o \( -path '*specs*' -o -path '*plans*' \) -print` in the workdir returned nothing. `git status --short` shows only "?? .hyperpowers/". `ls docs` shows only ui-guidelines.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: Listing every Skill tool_use with jq returned only {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. No plan files were found (same find command). The 15 grep hits for 'writing-plans' are text inside the loaded skill content, not invocations.

criteria.criterion: Asked approval of layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: The agent asked "Take a look and tell me what you think here." After my pick and the follow-ups it ended the chat design with "Does this look right? I'll start once you say yes." No Edit or Write to public/ files happened before that; git status shows the repo files unchanged.

criteria.criterion: After pick, began implementation or stated it would
criteria.evidence: The agent stated "I'll start once you say yes". After my "Yes, looks good — go ahead." it started implementation prep, re-reading the guideline sections (01-foundations token tables, 02/03/04) needed for the commits it described. I exited before any source edits landed.
